1.web: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
1.asv: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

2.web: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
2.asv: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; vanity of vanities, all is vanity.

3.web: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
3.asv: What profit hath man of all his labor wherein he laboreth under the sun?

4.web: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
4.asv: One generation goeth, and another generation cometh; but the earth abideth for ever.

5.web: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
5.asv: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to its place where it ariseth.

6.web: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
6.asv: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it turneth about continually in its course, and the wind returneth again to its circuits.

7.web: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
7.asv: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full; unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again.

8.web: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
8.asv: All things are full of weariness; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

9.web: That which has been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
9.asv: That which hath been is that which shall be; and that which hath been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

10.web: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new?” It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
10.asv: Is there a thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been long ago, in the ages which were before us.

11.web: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
11.asv: There is no remembrance of the former generations; neither shall there be any remembrance of the latter generations that are to come, among those that shall come after.

12.web: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
12.asv: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

13.web: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
13.asv: And I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven: it is a sore travail that God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.

14.web: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
14.asv: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.

15.web: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
15.asv: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

16.web: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
16.asv: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I have gotten me great wisdom above all that were before me in Jerusalem; yea, my heart hath had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

17.web: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
17.asv: And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also was a striving after wind.

18.web: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
18.asv: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
